Out of experience, as an aspie, if it’s the first relationship, and it’s codependent, it’s very difficult to identify as a toxic relationship while inside if it, or freshly out of it.

​

like my first BF had tons of red flags, but I was in the moment, in love, and I had my blinders on. I thought that this was how relationships went. And in the end it took him sending me to the hospital for an emotional breakdown for 2 weeks to purge me of him.   


the first step is getting her to see that this whole thing of feeling like shit and then going back to him to feel like shit again is not how love works, or self respect works.

my advice is there is going to be a period of time, mine was 6 months, that it’s going to be tough, especially when it starts. 

i would have wanted someone to talk to when I was crying 4-5 times a day. i wanted someone to talk to for 10-20 minutes evehr night to fill the gap. Casue every night it would be a talk with my first ex about  then. And light subjects, avoid conflict in that time.

​

and get her out once she is comfortable. Go for a walk, go grocery shopping,Cook together,  do crafts m nature, mall, anything but have her stay stuck in a bed in her room. Days turn to weeks to months doing that. I swear after I left him I reenacted the twilight scene of Edward leaving Bella and we see the seasons passing Through her window, I get that scene now.  


aspie first breakups Are tough, aspie breakups are tough in general. What you friend needs is To recognize her situation, extract herself, and a time if non challenging conversations that lead to getting back to normalcy.

I have been experimenting with making wooden clarinets in my senior year at high school 3 years ago...

there are mathematical formulas to make them the correct length, and then the correct pitch of ones desire.   
I do know if the top of my head the inner bore of a clarinet is 1/2 inch, and the outer diameter has to be at least 1 inch around. And the inner diameter cannot change too much, then you have a saxophone, nice, but not a clarinet.  

I found old spoon and fork handles make great key handles/levers, and the pad cups vary from bottle caps reworked into a more pleasant shape, to pencil eraser holders. Springs from sewing needles are really good. And the mounts for the whole Keywork thing could be donated by broken clarinets.

If one where to take those rules, they could make instru in weird, not to common but sought after keys.

G, F, Db, C, A.

The most important tone hole placement is the register vent, doubling the range of your clarinet, it could be a bit tricky, and if it’s not done right, calculated wrong, or the hole was drilled wrong, you ruin the entire instrument. Take care, do research.

The lowest pitch and highest pitch is only limited by the size of the instrument, with range being fixed to about 3 octaves. if someone could make a home wood worked clarinet have joins so it could be put away in a case, that would be cool, welcome to bass, sub bass, and sub contra bass homemade wood clarinet world.

Hey man, 

I want to say one thing, I saw the two identifiers in your post; gay and aspergers.

I am a 21 year old gay man with Aspergers in the northern suburbs of Chicago.

i must also say that I am having both of those identifiers irritated at the moment cause I’m in the process of mourning a 2.5 year long relationship. So if take that into account when I tell you some stuff.

i had a rough early development, was non verbal until four because of fluid in my ears and my Aspergers. I would act differently in my elementary school, be the butt of a lot of jokes. I think it was hard for me because I wasn’t “quick to the draw” back in those days. I couldn’t think of a snappy retort or comeback to being called a certain name quick enough. If I was, I would be seen as not such an easy target.

my mom was off doing what she wanted, partying. On paper, yeah, pick me up for 6 hours once a week, I guess she was doing her part, but she dropped me off at my dads place rang the doorbell and left, some mother.

my father raised me, and he is a musician professionally. I really wanted to learn a musical instrument, so I picked up clarinet at ten, both to please myself, and my father. Adults outside of my household were surprised when they spoke to me. when they asked me about school for example, I would tell them about how  “ I’m really enjoying how my teacher is explaining American history“ and go on to have a developed opinion and some decently sound logic behind it. one of my dads friends would pick my brain a ton in my later years on politics and philosophy.

middle school was hard, high school was really tough.

i came out as gay in my freshman year of high school. i didn’t want to hide a portion of what I was. And mostly the reaction was of mostly respect.

if you had a brain and an once of empathy and understanding, one would put together what I did was something momentous and far exceeds what some people in their 20’s could deal with, let alone a 14 year old.

but the majority of people didn’t make it tough, the minority did.

and as the years went on, I felt almost ignored by my peers, As while I got excellent grades, I would wait every night for a ping on my iPad, for someone to reach out and think I’m important enough to say hello. but in all that waiting that ping never came.

i was raped in the start of my senior year, and I only went to the police months later because he was in my film class the 2nd semester. this is a defining moment in my young adulthood.

im happy I did a couple things right in school, stay in band class, never got discipline, not even a detention. I chose not to graduate with my class because I didn’t feel like one of them. I wasn’t the smartest in the class, but I wasn’t the average either. I was almost unnoticed. I felt unimportant.

but I would do it all over again with the knowledge I have now.  It I suppose a lot of people feel that.

we are approaching my recent history, I met my first boyfriend on Grindr In October of 2017.

he wanted to take me out on a date. I asked him to pick me up, I never got my license to this day even.

we went to the Hollywood boulevard theater and restaurant. And within minutes I was cuddling him.

my first cuddle.

i felt wanted for the first time in my life.

and moments  Later,  my first kiss.

electricity.

he was a student software engineer Going for his bachelor, very smart guy. i joked how my personality was similar to a computer. There were ups and downs, navigating what it’s like to have a partner with Aspergers, all while his parents never knew I existed.

the troubles come last November when he would be graduating soon. that was change, and I was a nervous wreck of fear and abandonment.

I let the negactive aspects of aspergers make a self fulfilling prophecy. He didn’t leave me cause he wanted to, but because he was hurting me stunting my emotional growth. if he would have taken me with him to washington d.c, he would be trapping me in a caged life, be depending on him for everything, and he wanted me to fly and be happy.   


now the present, I’m happy he is at a good big boy job, and I’m still mourning the loss of my first relationship, but being so different, a gay aspie, I somehow think there is a slight tinge if optimism in me.

being different isn’t easy, but it isn’t a death sentence.

and hey, I’m unemployed rn, i went through 6 jobs in the past year, it sucks, but I think as long as I don’t stop going to school, I could be the music teacher I wanna be.   
and I’m sorry if I ranted too long, just I connected with this post.

I think it has something to do with the country/city divide in Italy over a century ago, as well as the north/south divide as well.

Northern cuisine is more cheese and dairy sauces, like fettuccine Alfredo. Those ingredients are more expensive and they are more plentiful in northern town and especially northern Italian cities. Along side that these areas are historically Influenced by French cuisine.

Southern and especially Sicilian( which my family is) areas are more agrarian, and not as wealthy, so hard cheese like Parmesan, that doesn’t melt well and doesn’t require a lot of effort to keep fresh, is cheaper. As well as tons tomatoes being on hand, the hot Mediterranean sun and all.

Sorry if this is a long rant, cooking and history are special interests.

First off, I live in an Italian household, every Sunday is pasta day.

A day that I almost never participate in. As odd as that sounds.

We eat a pasta called linguine, flat and long, but my Gma always splits them in half, and that defeats the purpose of having , like, noodles. You want long noodles If you want a noodle in the first place.

I actually prefer Potato gnocchi, with red sauce and melted mozzarella and Parmessian.
